cases.exposure_context_quote: A 53-year-old male agricultural worker presented approximately 3 h after ingesting an unknown pesticide.
cases.agent_quote: Subsequently, relatives produced the pesticide container revealing Amitraz (125 mg/mL formulation) (Taktic 12.5% EC [MSD Animal Health, Pune, India])
cases.circumstance: Ingested an unknown pesticide (later identified as amitraz); intent and setting not stated; gastric lavage with activated charcoal at local care.

symptoms.quote: On arrival, he was obtunded (Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS] 9/15) with bilaterally constricted pupils

On arrival, he was obtunded (Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS] 9/15) with bilaterally constricted pupils ... The neurological status declined; GCS dropped to 4/15, pupils dilated, and respiratory effort weakened.
unrecordable blood pressure, bradycardia at 56 beats per min, and oxygen saturation around 85% on room air
Arterial blood gas revealed type II respiratory failure; he was intubated and ventilated.

symptoms.finding: absence of excessive secretions and diarrhea
symptoms.quote: Excessive secretions and diarrhea were absent.

labs.name: serum cholinesterase
labs.quote: Serum cholinesterase was normal, excluding OP poisoning.

labs.name: CBC/LFTs
labs.value: mild leukocytosis and elevated liver enzymes
labs.quote: Laboratory tests showed mild leukocytosis and elevated liver enzymes.

treatment.name: gastric lavage with activated charcoal (local care)
treatment.quote: Initial local care included gastric lavage with activated charcoal.

treatment.name: atropine 6 mg IV and oxygen therapy
treatment.quote: Based on miosis and bradycardia, atropine intravenous 6 mg was given with oxygen therapy.

treatment.name: dopamine infusion for persistent hypotension
treatment.quote: Despite fluid resuscitation, hypotension persisted, requiring dopamine infusion.

treatment.name: intubation and ventilation (extubated at 96 h)
treatment.quote: Arterial blood gas revealed type II respiratory failure; he was intubated and ventilated. Support continued over 4 days with gradual recovery and successful extubation at 96 h.

cases.icu_admission: UNVERIFIED (intubated and ventilated for 4 days; formal ICU admission not stated)
cases.outcome: Gradual recovery with successful extubation at 96 hours
cases.outcome_quote: Support continued over 4 days with gradual recovery and successful extubation at 96 h.
cases.notes: Amitraz poisoning mimicking organophosphate toxicity; normal cholinesterase and absent secretory features were distinguishing clues.

cases.exposure_context_quote: A 21-year-old male presented 3 h after ingestion of a rodenticide identified initially as “Khatnil spray” containing 1% Propoxur (a carbamate) (Hindustan Insecticides Ltd., New Delhi, India).
cases.agent: fipronil (0.05% fipronil gel; initially misidentified as propoxur 'Khatnil spray')
cases.agent_quote: Detailed history and analysis identified the agent as 0.05% Fipronil gel (Ankur Chemicals, Maharashtra, India).
cases.circumstance: Ingestion 3 h before presentation; product initially identified as propoxur rodenticide, later identified as fipronil gel; intent and setting not stated.

symptoms.quote: He had vomiting, altered mental status (GCS E2V2M3), bradycardia (58 bpm), bilateral miosis, respiratory distress, coarse crepitations, and abundant oral secretions.

treatment.name: intubation and ventilation
treatment.quote: Due to airway compromise, he was intubated and ventilated.

treatment.name: supportive care
treatment.quote: Improvement followed supportive care and atropine, with extubation at 18 h.

cases.exposure_context_quote: A 32-year-old male exposed to pesticide ingestion and treated with atropine at a peripheral hospital presented with vomiting, altered sensorium, bradycardia (52 bpm), hypotension (90/60 mmHg), respiratory distress, excessive secretions, constricted reactive pupils, and decreased muscle tone.
cases.agent: 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) herbicide (United Phosphorus Ltd., Mumbai, India)
cases.agent_quote: Family confirmed ingestion of 2,4-D herbicide (United Phosphorus Ltd., Mumbai, India).
cases.circumstance: Ingestion; treated with atropine at a peripheral hospital before presentation; intent and setting not stated.

symptoms.quote: presented with vomiting, altered sensorium, bradycardia (52 bpm), hypotension (90/60 mmHg), respiratory distress, excessive secretions, constricted reactive pupils, and decreased muscle tone.
presented with vomiting, altered sensorium, bradycardia (52 bpm), hypotension (90/60 mmHg), respiratory distress, excessive secretions, constricted reactive pupils, and decreased muscle tone.

symptoms.finding: respiratory distress with excessive secretions and constricted pupils

labs.name: creatine phosphokinase (CPK)
labs.quote: Laboratory investigations showed markedly elevated creatine phosphokinase (CPK) (12,400 U/L), metabolic acidosis, and normal cholinesterase.

labs.name: cholinesterase
labs.quote: Laboratory investigations showed markedly elevated creatine phosphokinase (CPK) (12,400 U/L), metabolic acidosis, and normal cholinesterase.

treatment.name: intravenous hydration and urinary alkalinization with sodium bicarbonate
treatment.quote: He received intravenous hydration and urinary alkalinization with sodium bicarbonate.

cases.outcome: Neurological and lab parameters improved over 72 h; discharged in good condition
cases.outcome_quote: Over 72 h, neurological and lab parameters improved, and he was discharged in good condition.
cases.notes: 2,4-D poisoning mimicking organophosphate toxicity; elevated CPK, metabolic acidosis and normal cholinesterase were key distinguishing features.
